quest.title: The Truest Thing
quest.description: With the Phantom Weasel arrested, Lyney's show can finally take place. Fingers crossed that everything goes smoothly...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Watch the magic show at the opera house

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, Paimon's excited to see another of Lyney's magic shows. Wait... Lynette, shouldn't you be on stage by now?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Not this time. My brother's going solo today.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: So I'll be watching with you.

dialogues.speaker: Robert Houdin
dialogues.text: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen! I hope everybody's ready, because the show is about to begin!

dialogues.speaker: Robert Houdin
dialogues.text: The great magician Lyney has prepared a spectacular show for us all tonight, concluding with an all-new grand finale that no audience has ever seen before!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! A new trick!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Thank you all so much for coming. Now, prepare to join me on a journey through the mystical and miraculous.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Lyney wows the audience with his skill...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Exciting stuff, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Yes, it's just... It reminds me of him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder. Cesar was a famous magician, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So how did you two first meet, Jemma?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Hmm? Well, I was out on the street once, and I saw him performing for little children.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Children love magic, because they're willing to believe in things that can't be rationally explained. Cesar had this amazing way of bringing them into a dream-like world.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: And somehow... I felt drawn to him, too. So I went up and asked him to do a trick for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, that sounds so romantic... What trick did he do?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: It was... with a flower. He took it in his hand, snapped his fingers, and it magically appeared on my head.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: I was so happy that day. No one had ever given me a flower before that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, that's so cute... Actually, now that you mention it, Lyney's done that one before.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Is that right? Then I suppose he's a romantic at heart, just like Cesar. So let's treasure the time we have with him.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: After all... You never know when the people dearest to you might... be gone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. It's all over now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Paimon doesn't really know how to comfort you, but at the very least, no one's gonna be intimidating you from now on. You can breathe easy at least, right?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: ...Right.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Yes, you can breathe easy now, Phantom Weasel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See, even Lynette says— Wait, what!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Phantom Weasel? Lorenzo escaped? Where is he?

response.speaker: Jemma
response.text: Wh—What do you mean, "Phantom Weasel"?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: As Lyney once said... A performer's job is to commit fully to their role, and put on a flawless performance for their audience.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: But once the bag of tricks is empty, and the curtain falls, it's time to end the show. The spotlight is no place for someone with no more cards up their sleeve.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: It's been ten years, Jemma. Aren't you tired of the grieving widow act? I think it's time to put an end to it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you talking about? Paimon doesn't like this riddle...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon doesn't like where this is going... C'mon, say something!

response.speaker: Robert Houdin
response.text: Ladies and Gentlemen! I hope you're all enjoying the performance so far!

response.speaker: Robert Houdin
response.text: There will now be a brief intermission, after which Lyney will perform the most electrifying act of tonight's show — the one we've all been waiting for!

response.speaker: Robert Houdin
response.text: The final performance will take place outside of the opera house, so please make your way outside in a calm and orderly fashion.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: The Phantom Weasel never did like public places, did they?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Don't worry, this place will be quiet soon. Let's talk somewhere else for now.

talks.objective: Go somewhere quiet and ask about the truth

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Dear me, this is awkward, isn't it? And unfortunately, I'm all out of gadgets, so I'm afraid I can't do any tricks to liven up the mood.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: This is a big mistake for a magician to make. But thankfully, I do have a backup plan... Now, who wants to hear a story?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Lyney, don't we have more important things to address right now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lynette accused Jemma of being the real Phantom Weasel a moment ago. What the heck's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: All in good time. Magicians are good at guessing what people are thinking. I know the questions you want to ask... and as it happens, the story I'm about to tell might answer a few of them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Well then, let's hear it! Paimon's dying of curiosity here!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Let's go back to the very beginning. A decade ago, when The Phantom Weasel was terrorizing the Court of Fontaine. She never missed a target, never left a trace, and no treasure was safe from her thieving hands.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But as her infamy grew, so did the readiness of the police, and her opportunities to act became ever fewer. Every day, she ran the risk of being exposed for who she was.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Of course, she could not simply take this lying down, and before long she found her ticket to freedom: She would create a scapegoat, a false Weasel to close the chapter on her behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: After weighing her options, she set her sights on a renowned magician — Cesar. After all, magic and theft shared enough similarities for people to buy the story when the "truth" came out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... So then what?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Being the master deceiver she was, The Weasel easily earned Cesar's trust. Now all that remained was to frame him for her countless crimes.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: But as she was considering how to make her move, she noticed Cesar's aggrieved pupil, and a new thought entered her mind: "Maybe I don't need to get my hands dirty after all"...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: At her encouragement, Lorenzo tampered with Cesar's magic box, causing him to fall to his death.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Afterwards, Lorenzo seized his master's property, and The Weasel set about tarnishing Cesar's reputation. Two co-conspirators committed the perfect crime.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: I've gotta hand it to you, you're both exceptional storytellers. It's enough to make even me wonder whether there was really another mastermind behind all this, pulling the strings.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: But I just have one question. You seem to think that I am the villain in this tale. What's brought this on, Lyney? Is it something that Lorenzo said?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Lorenzo said nothing at all.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But I never believed that he was The Weasel, and in fact my investigation only made me more certain of that. He was too forthcoming with his confession — as if there was something else he was trying to hide.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: How disappointing. So you'd sooner trust Lorenzo than me, even without a shred of evidence?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: A magician is an expert at playing the audience to get the result they want. And I have no doubt that you, Jemma, are equally talented in this regard.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: With a little help from Lorenzo, you put on a very convincing performance. The lovesick fiancée, whose devotion to her betrothed is unshakable even under threats of violence...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Cesar was maligned and hated by all for ten years, but you? Everyone sympathized with your plight.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Who would suspect for one second that the lovely young lady always seen weeping in front of Cesar's grave was actually the mastermind behind his demise? No, not that poor lady. Perish the thought!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you mean... The whole intimidation thing was just a hoax? Jemma and Lorenzo were both in on it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why would Lorenzo agree to that? And why didn't he sell her out, even at the end? Instead of admitting to being The Weasel himself...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes, why indeed? Maybe Jemma herself could enlighten us on that question.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Well, Lyney, if you're so confident in your version of events, then I think the answer should be obvious.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Having killed Cesar with his own hands, Lorenzo was plagued by overwhelming guilt.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Revealing The Phantom Weasel's true identity would serve no purpose. But if the Weasel remained free, then she could take care of Lorenzo's loved ones.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: An excellent answer... Though sadly, a little dull.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Is that right? Well don't let me bore you. If you'd care to change the topic to something more interesting, I'd be much obliged.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: As a matter of fact, there's one thing I'd really like to understand.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Why would the real Weasel have targeted things that only have value to other people? Could you shed any light on that?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Of course. After all, we're just telling stories here, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: If I had to guess, I would say that the real Weasel must have had a terrible childhood.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Left to fend for herself after her parents died young. Betrayed. Scorned. Beaten...

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: She'd scrounge waste paper from garbage bins to draw on, using twigs and dirt for lack of ink and pen. She'd sew ugly ragdolls from whatever scrap material she could get her hands on.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: This was her only source of happiness in life. But it was all she needed, and she was content... until the world decided that even this was too good for her.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Once again, she was betrayed, and this time everything was taken from her. She felt like life was a miry pit that dragged her further down the more she struggled to escape. At that tender age, she should have been happy... Instead, she stood in the shadows and watched with envy as all good things in the world passed her by.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: This was a fate too cruel for anyone to bear. Her pain became a breeding ground for dark thoughts, thoughts which festered and grew into a twisted solution to her troubles:

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: "I detest the happiness of others in all its forms alike."

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: "I will rob them of everything they hold to be good and true, and it will fill the void in my soul."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's some pretty heavy stuff...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: ...Now it all makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Does this story satisfy you, Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes, it is quite to my tastes. Thank you for helping to clear up my confusion.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So what was with the warning letter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that's right. What drove you to write that letter, Jemma? What were you trying to achieve there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cause without that, none of this would have ever come to light...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: She didn't write the letter.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: After ten long years, I'd hoped that The Phantom Weasel would be consigned to the history books by now. But it seems like someone still wasn't ready to let her finally be at peace.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Lyney... Or should I call you The Phantom Copycat now? You were the one who posted that letter outside the opera house. But why?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Very sharp, Phantom Weasel. Still as shrewd as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, no need for me to be coy about it. Our goal was to clear Cesar's name.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The most straightforward way to change the public's impression of Cesar was to force The Weasel to show themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: That's it? You had no other agenda?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Of course we did. We made it quite clear in the letter, I believe? "I shall take from you that which you hold most dear, just as you did to me ten years ago."

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Ten years ago...? You mean Cesar's death? You... met him?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Wait... Oh, I get it! You were those two obnoxious kids! It's been so long, and you're all grown up now... I didn't recognize you.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: He taught you magic back then, didn't he? For what, ten days or something? ...And you went to all this trouble... why, because you feel like you still owe him something?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We remember all our debts, however great or small.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ten years ago, Cesar's reputation was torn to shreds and his legacy was thrown out. Ten years on, and no one cares what the truth is anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But we did not forget, and so we came to find you.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: And? What exactly did you take from me? I'm still standing, as you can see. Lorenzo has admitted to everything — I'm free.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: "Free"? ...Do you really think so?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Cesar once told me that even though the world is filled with lies and falsehoods, we must find our own truth.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I think that applies to you, too. Truth can take many forms — prized possessions with nostalgic value, fervent hopes and dreams... and irreplaceable people.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Life took many things from you, and those wounds never healed. When they ached unbearably in the dead of night, stealing became your way of numbing the pain.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I'm saying that for the last ten years, you've been living a rather uneventful life. Perhaps that's because you've found something other than a life of crime to fill the hole?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Back to Lorenzo for a second: He murdered his own master, played along with your act, and took pains to make sure any suspicion would be directed towards him. But what did he have to gain from all that?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: He knew who you were and the things you'd done, and despite that, he was willing to give everything up for your sake. He's the reason that you haven't felt the compulsion to steal in all these years.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You're more than just accomplices in murder — you're the only real friends each other has. So I think you know, deep down, that he is the only "truth" you have in your life.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But that truth is gone now. And I guarantee you, you'll never see it again.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Congratulations on your freedom, Jemma.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Your freedom will cost you dearly. From now on, you'll be all alone in a world full of lies and falsehoods. I do hope you'll be able to bear it — you've still got a long life ahead of you, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Robert Houdin
dialogues.text: Gather 'round, one and all, the time has now come for the amazing Lyney to perform his final act in tonight's show!

dialogues.speaker: Robert Houdin
dialogues.text: I'm sure you're all wondering what he has planned for the grand finale? Well, wonder no more, for the answer is... A death-defying high-altitude escape!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A high-altitude escape!?

response.speaker: Robert Houdin
response.text: I'm sure you all remember the magician Cesar. This was the very trick that led to his fatal fall, after which he was dubbed The Phantom Weasel.

response.speaker: Robert Houdin
response.text: But we have now learned that Cesar was wrongly accused, and that the real Weasel has now confessed to their crimes...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Guess that's my cue to leave. Whew... I've been practicing this one for ages now, but I'm still a little nervous.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I hope you enjoy the rest of the show. There may be a lot of people watching tonight, but you alone are my true witnesses.

response.speaker: Jemma
response.text: Lyney, wait.

response.speaker: Jemma
response.text: You two hid a lot from Cesar — he went to his grave without ever knowing your secrets. So what about now? Are you an open book — or are you still the same as ever?

response.speaker: Jemma
response.text: You don't have to tell lies to end up isolated and alone. One day, you'll end up exactly where I am today — maybe then you'll finally understand.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You're wrong. I'm nothing like you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, uh... What are we, uh... doing now?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Like Lyney said — when you're ready, let's head outside and watch the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what about Jemma...?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: She'll figure out what's best for her soon enough. Oh — and if you'd like to see Lyney after the show... You know where he'll be. The usual haunt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, well let's go and watch Lyney's finale then! This trick's a pretty dangerous one... but he should be able to pull it off, right?

choices.text: The trick that Cesar died attempting...

dialogues.speaker: Janet
dialogues.text: Did you see that? One minute he was falling... And the next, he turned into flowers!

dialogues.speaker: Randolf
dialogues.text: How could he possibly have done that?

dialogues.speaker: Olivia
dialogues.text: How mysterious! I didn't blink once, he just... vanished, right in front of my eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: What a heart-stopping magic show! This was really worth the trip.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Cesar's name has finally been cleared, and Fontaine's new star magician, Lyney, has fulfilled a wish on his behalf... Ah, I couldn't ask for a better grand finale. It will make a great headline for The Steambird tomorrow, even if I do say so myself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... Looks like everyone really loved Lyney's grand finale!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Even though they don't know the full story...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't see Lyney anywhere. Where'd he go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Lynette said he'd be waiting for us at the "usual haunt"... But, um... Where is that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The cemetery...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean the one where Cesar's buried?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's probably it. This whole magic show kinda seemed like Lyney's way of saying goodbye to Cesar. So it makes sense that that's where he'd be afterward.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's go look for him there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney, there you are!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright? Paimon was scared to death when the chain broke... Paimon was sure something had gone horribly wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Magic is a performance art. A magician has to get creative to keep the audience on tenterhooks — that's our job. So I tweaked Cesar's original setup a little to keep it fresh.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I was honestly a little nervous during the live performance. The thought of falling, suddenly feeling weightless, seeing the sky and the ground spinning and spinning...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Sometimes, I can't help but wonder what Cesar thought in those final moments.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Did he regret taking Jemma and Lorenzo on? Or... Did he believe that it was his own slip-up right until the end?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know... Paimon's been wanting to ask you about something ever since we were in Cesar's workshop. You learned magic from Cesar once, didn't you? When was that?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: After I joined the House of the Hearth. To be honest, Lynette and I had an agenda when we approached him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An agenda?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I told you about my past before, remember? As a young boy, I survived by secretly learning magic from street performers. I'd watch their tricks and try to figure out how they were done.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But I quickly realized that observation alone could only get me so far. What I saw was the polished final performance, but the rigorous training they put in behind the scenes remained invisible to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I needed to learn how to improve my sleight of hand, hone my misdirection skills, and make niftier props...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We were gifted enough that we'd made some progress by ourselves. But without proper guidance from a professional magician, we quickly plateaued.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's why you sought Cesar out?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes. We figured there was no harm in asking — but it took us by surprise that he was so willing to teach us.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: In all, we only spent ten short days together, but he was very good to us. By contrast, we hid so many things from him...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: For instance, when he asked why I wanted to learn magic... I answered "It's my passion."

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But in truth, there was already a lot more to the story by then. After being taken in by an aristocrat for our magic talent, then betrayed soon after... This was no longer about me doing what I loved.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: What amazed me was how the lie escaped my lips even as I was hesitating over whether to tell him the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Trust is a beautiful thing. Sadly, I'd forgotten how to trust by then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Still worried about the way I feel? You really are a gentle soul, aren't you?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But don't worry, I'm used to it now. From the mansions of the elite to the House of the Hearth, lies and selfishness have followed me and Lynette everywhere we go.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: After Cesar went on tour, we became busy with our missions. The next we heard of him was that he'd fallen to his death and was now declared to be The Phantom Weasel...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That night, I remembered his smile... But as I lay there, I didn't know what to say to him.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: To keep secrets is to put up walls. The longer you keep them up, the less you let people in. Then one day, you look around and realize your life is like an empty auditorium after a show — full of seats once occupied by all the people who left... But I guess that's the price we have to pay.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You only realize how much someone really meant to you when you lose them completely. That's why I was so confident this would hurt Jemma... because I've felt it for myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Cheer up, Lyney.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've had to say our fair share of goodbyes during our journey, too... But whatever happens, Paimon always believes in what tomorrow brings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Delicious food, fun toys, and {NICKNAME} by my side... Paimon just needs to focus on things like this, and all the unhappy stuff goes right out the window.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Y'know, {NICKNAME}... Doesn't that kinda make you Paimon's "truth"?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Exactly. It's the same for me and Lynette — we are the truest thing each other has in the world, and nothing can replace that.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Life has taken plenty from us, like it did from Jemma. But at least it left us with each other. That's what gave us the strength to get through the darkest days.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's why the darkness never consumed me, and why it never will. Maybe we live in the shadows too, but we remember every precious ray of light that shines through.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Alright, time to lighten this conversation up a little! What did you think of the show tonight? Were you happy with it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It was amazing! Paimon just wishes we hadn't been so distracted with the Jemma situation... We spent most of our time in the opera house just talking, and pretty much missed the entire first half of the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Lyney... Could you do just one more trick for us?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Whoa, that's a bit of a tall order I'm afraid. The show's just finished, so my sleeves are decidedly card-free right now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, c'mon... Surely you can think of something! The Lyney Paimon knows can do anything if he puts his mind to it!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh, alright then. I'll give it a go — but only because it's you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Watch closely. I have a flower in my hand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You liar! There's nothing in your hand! We ain't going along with this!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Huh? My goodness, you're right! But I could've sworn I brought one here with me... Okay, try this. Count down with me: Three, two, one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Three, two, one!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Now have another look around — maybe the flower's appeared somewhere else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Let's see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, there it is! This is a different flower from the one last time, right? This one's called... oh yeah, a Rainbow Rose!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But more importantly — Paimon has to know how the trick is done! Please, Lyney, pretty please?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, if you want to learn magic, you'll have to start by addressing me as "Teacher"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Fine, pleeease, Teacher, please!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: *sigh* Since you asked so nicely... I'll share one little tip with you. Namely, the student of magic cannot solely rely on others being prepared to reveal their secrets. You have to observe, think, and find the answers for yourself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Is that it!?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, look at the time — we shouldn't linger here too long. Thanks again for coming to see my show. I bid you both good night!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...I look forward to seeing you again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, fine... See ya!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shall we head back now too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon can't wait to read The Steambird tomorrow. Paimon bets Lyney and Cesar will be plastered all over it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's head to The Steambird's offices tomorrow morning and see what we can find out!

choices.text: We're in your "auditorium," and we're not going anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: It may take some time, but Cesar's reputation will be restored now that the real culprit has been captured.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Looks like Jemma chose a good man after all...

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: ...I've spoken many choice words about Cesar over the years.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: I'm so ashamed of myself now. He was such a good man...

dialogues.speaker: Dolora
dialogues.text: I can't believe Lorenzo was intimidating Jemma all this time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you met Lorenzo before?

dialogues.speaker: Dolora
dialogues.text: He comes around here sometimes. Not to clean Cesar's grave, though. He just stands off to the side and watches Jemma from a distance.

dialogues.speaker: Dolora
dialogues.text: She must've known, but she never asked him to leave. I wonder why that is.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Here I am, as we agreed!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I wonder what kind of show Lyney has prepared for us this time? Oh, the anticipation, it's killing me!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, and how could I forget — thank you both for capturing Lorenzo. Now that this decade-long case of The Phantom Weasel has finally been put to rest, I'm gonna go through my notes and put it all together into the most spectacular special column piece to ever grace the pages of The Steambird!

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: What is my truth...?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Sometimes, I think I'm like a gambling addict... All I care about is winning, and it doesn't matter what's at stake.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: By the time I come to my senses, I'm left with nothing. Oh, if I had my time again...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Magicians are not like thieves.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Thieves only tear things apart. But good-hearted magicians... They put things back together.
